read_by: .github/ci/ci_gate.py -- see its module docstring for the format contract

measured.condition: the real thing: GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest, run 32021100181, first push of task/p0.10-reproducibility, workflow as committed (pinned threads, dev extra only, CityFlow not built, no corpus, no SUMO binary)
measured.result: 1 failed, 891 passed, 72 skipped (964 collected). The failure is UNRELATED to the ceiling -- see docs/returns/P0.10.md: offline/rtg_calibration.py asserts a committed p-value reproduces exactly, and it differs by 1 ulp on the runner.
measured.breakdown: 32 cityflow-gated + 28 corpus/checkpoint-gated + 10 SUMO/traci-gated + 2 matplotlib = 72, counted from the run's own -rs block

superseded.why_it_was_wrong: It came from a simulated runner on the dev machine, and the simulation was defeated by usrmerge: the harness removed `sumo` from a symlink copy of /usr/bin but left /bin on PATH, and /bin IS /usr/bin on this system, so shutil.which('sumo') kept finding it and 10 SUMO-gated tests ran that a runner skips. The error was invisible locally and was caught by the first real run -- which is the reason the ceiling was declared provisional and the branch was pushed.

ceiling_is_a_consequence_of: the workflow does NOT build the vendored CityFlow (coordinator ruling 2026-08-17: an unverified C++ build step is a new failure surface on the one task whose purpose is reliability). 32 of these 72 skips are cityflow-gated, so building it would move the ceiling from 72 to 40.

no corpus is available on a runner: datasets*/ is gitignored and ~189 MB, so 28 corpus- and checkpoint-gated tests skip. That 28 independently reproduces the coordinator's 2026-08-16 corpus-absent measurement.

SUMO is not installed on the runner, so _sumo_available() is False and 10 SUMO-backed tests skip cleanly. sumolib IS present -- traci declares sumolib>=1.27.1 and pip resolved it -- so the gate here is the missing binary, not the missing module.
the workflow installs the dev extra only, so the 2 matplotlib-gated tests skip.

re_measure_required_at.reason: P5.1 adds tests that skip without a corpus. It measured 984 passed, 53 skipped corpus-absent in its own tree on 2026-08-17, against 898 passed, 28 skipped for the same condition on main -- roughly +25 skips. This ceiling WILL breach on that merge, and it is meant to: the job goes red and prints the observed number.
re_measure_required_at.mandated_by: coordinator ruling on BRIEF_23 Q1, 2026-08-17 -- 'a ceiling whose expiry lives only in a chat is a ceiling that silently breaches'

pytest.how_to_update: Read the observed count from the failing job's summary, re-measure deliberately, and commit the new value together with the reason in the same commit. Never widen it with slack: slack is what blinds the gate.

hygiene.why_not_zero: DEFERRED 45: 16 pre-existing TH006 findings in four frozen-adjacent test files. They are recorded, not tolerated silently, and they may NOT be 'fixed' to make CI green -- the files are next to frozen code and the fix is a task of its own. Re-measured for P0.10 from the full output of a no-argument run on 2026-08-17: 16, matching the coordinator's four independent counts.

english.why_not_zero: P0.9, still open: the o-acute false positive. Three of these five are the guard's own documentation of the character class it detects, quoted in claude_guard.sh and in two committed patches; de-diacriticising them would corrupt a record. Measured for P0.10 on 2026-08-17: 5.

frozen_guard.why: The guard derives everything from `git status --porcelain`, which is clean on a fresh checkout, so on a runner it always passes and proves nothing. It is invoked anyway because its absence would be worse, and the workflow says so at the call site rather than letting a green tick imply more than it proves. A PR-diff variant is a NEW enforcement mechanism and needs its own authorisation -- coordinator ruling 2026-08-17, parked as a DEFERRED row.
